newsitem.title: HONG KONG: AsiaSat October launch on schedule.
newsitem.headline: AsiaSat October launch on schedule.

text.p: Asia Satellite Telecommunications Holdings Ltd is keeping to its schedule to launch its third geostationary satellite in October, senior executives said on Tuesday.
"There is no problem with Proton (launch vehicle) or the manufacturer," said chief executive Peter Jackson.
"We have a (time) slot in October, that is the first slot, but it could be moved."

The satellite, a Hughes HS 601 HP model, was being built by Hughes Electronics Corp of the United States and would be launched by a Russian Proton D-1-e rocket from the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan, a company statement said.
That satellite, AsiaSat 3, would take up the geostationary orbit of AsiaSat 1 at 105.5 degrees east.
"It will be co-located with (AsiaSat) One initially and eventually it (AsiaSat 1) will be moved away," Jackson said.
AsiaSat 1 would come to the end of its nine-year life in 1999, but AsiaSat 3 would take over the operations of AsiaSat 1 in advance.
"AsiaSat 3 is much more powerful and has a much much broader footprint," said Jackson.
"The insurance is in place. We got a very favourable rate for that, and so basically we are very confident that we will be within budget for that AsiaSat 3 project," said Jackson.

AsiaSat 3 has 28 C-band transponders and 16 ku-band transponders, larger than the 24 C-band transponders of AsiaSat 1. The company is now marketing the extra capacity of those four extra C-band and 16 ku-bank transponders.
"We have not signed with anyone yet, but we are in negotiations with several people," said Jackson.
The company is expected to finalise an agreement to purchase an in-orbit satellite, currently located at 122 degrees east, next month.
This position would be the future location of AsiaSat 4, when it is launched in 1999, the company said.
The cost of that purchase was originally estimated at US$20 million but it was likely to be less than that, said Jackson.
The company said it is still seeking proposals from manufacturers for the building of AsiaSat 4.
On Wednesday, Asia Satellite, which was listed in June 1996, reported profit attributable to shareholders of HK$395 million in 1996, an 134 percent increase over its 1995 pro forma results.
Cable and Wireless Plc, Hutchison Whampoa Ltd and CITIC Pacific each hold a 23.00 percent stake in the company.
Asia Satellite rose HK$0.30 to close at HK$19.70 on Tuesday.
